Noto

Site · Noto, Italy

The ancient city of Noto, on the plateau of Mount Alveria, was once home to a flourishing Jewish community which left the only known Sicilian siddur (prayer book); the book is now held at the Biblioteca Palatina in Parma (ref: msparmense 1741/de’ Rossi 570 ). The city was destroyed by an earthquake in 1693, and then rebuilt in its current position, in the Baroque style. The Noto Civic Archaeological Museum, contains a phylactery engraved on a limestone slab. Other magical phylacteries engraved on small metal plates are on display at the Archeological Museum in Santa Croce Camerina (Ragusa).
